rules.law_name: Newark Ban the Box Housing Ordinance
rules.title: Criminal-history screening restrictions for rental housing applicants
rules.requirement: For Newark rental housing, landlords and real estate brokers may inquire into or consider an applicant’s criminal history only after a formal application and must give written notice before conducting a criminal history inquiry. The ordinance limits what criminal records may be considered, requires consideration of rehabilitation and other factors, requires written adverse-action notice with results, keeps criminal-history information confidential, and bars ads referencing criminal-history screening.
rules.key_value: Inquiry only after formal application; 8-year indictable-offense lookback; 5-year disorderly-persons/municipal-violation lookback; 10 business days for adverse-action notice; fines up to $500 first violation and $1,000 subsequent violations

coverage.summary: Applies to rentals, leases, and subleases of real property in Newark, except a single apartment or flat in an owner-occupied two-family dwelling and room rentals in an owner-occupied one-family dwelling.

rules.exemptions: The prohibitions do not apply where federal or state law, regulation, or rule requires or permits consideration of criminal history, limited to the offenses and time periods that law permits or requires; they also do not apply to real property designated for a government program or obligation designed to encourage housing for individuals with criminal histories.
rules.penalty: A first violation is subject to a fine of up to $500; each subsequent violation is subject to a fine of up to $1,000.
rules.interaction: The ordinance preserves federally or state-required or permitted criminal-history screening, but only for the offenses, offense types, and time periods that the federal or state law, regulation, or rule allows.
rules.quoted_span:
Inquiry into and consideration of any applicant's criminal history shall take place only after the
            applicant has submitted a formal application.
